## The answer to your headline question

**The ledger says 0 items with no source. The true number is 3, and it is the same three results as before.**

`https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~aknapp/download/b2-alg-inside.pdf` **returns HTTP 404.** So does `download.html`, the book's own page, and `~aknapp/` itself. Verified with curl (http/https, browser UA, follow-redirects) and independently with WebFetch. Not a network artifact: `math.stonybrook.edu` root returns 200 with the live department site, and my control fetch of Axler in the same session returned 200 and 2.8 MB. Search engines still index the URL — that index is historical.

`lem-coprime-kernel-decomposition`, `cor-primary-projections-are-polynomials-in-the-endomorphism` and `ex-primary-decomposition-over-q-with-an-irreducible-quadratic` have **only** Knapp rows. Two more keep a live row weaker than the item: `thm-primary-decomposition-for-an-endomorphism`'s only non-Knapp backing is Axler 8.4 (the null/range split, not the irreducible-power decomposition), and `cor-generalised-eigenspace-decomposition-…` rests on Axler 8.22, which I read — it opens *"Suppose $\mathbf F = \mathbf C$."*

So the arbitrary-field primary decomposition still has no live source. **But this looks like a re-point, not a re-scope**: Project Euclid distributes the digital second edition with **Chapter V open access** — exactly the declared read range. The chapter link resolves; the PDF endpoint sits behind Incapsula, so it's human-openable but not machine-fetchable from here. Two McGill mirrors are live but serving at ~50 KB/s; a download is still in flight and I did **not** certify Knapp's content. If Chapter V turns out not to carry Theorem 5.19 at those pages, that's your call between restricting to the split case and sourcing it yourself.

## What the third pass got right

Axler is honest exhaustively — **53/53** numbered results present at their claimed numbers, page anchors exact (PDF 153 = printed 139 = Thm 5.18, and so on). Conrad *Potential Diagonalizability* is now in the ledger and all four rows check against the PDF. The Conrad locator now matches its enumeration. The `replacement_audit` survived at 22 rows. F3.4, F3.6, F3.7 all confirmed fixed — the simultaneous-diagonalisation title is a true iff with the converse proved and the diagonalisability hypothesis correctly in the subject; `splitting-fields` is in closure (37 → 38) and all five predicate uses cite the definition.

## Batch 7 meets the F7.1 standard on the corollary

Split hypothesis in, `def-algebraically-closed-field` out of deps, contract, input map and the entire batch; both consumer quotes repaired to carry their hypotheses; example over ℚ (I checked the basis argument — it works because $p \neq 0$ in ℚ, and would fail over $\mathbf F_p$); lemma removed with no orphan row; **and the provenance row moved with the statement.** F7.4 landed better than asked — the cited `thm-pascals-rule` quote *is* the hockey-stick identity. F7.5, F7.7, F7.8 all fixed.

Two declaration-level carry-forwards, not blockers: `ex-closed-walks-in-the-complete-graph` declares one dependency and uses three — it was re-based from ℂ to ℚ and left its walk-counting obligation behind, while every other walk example on the same B page declares that machinery. And the Stanley locator is still narrower than its enumeration, third pass running.

## Three things you should know

**F3.3 is now a coverage gap, not a preference.** Inside Conrad's declared range, immediately after Cor 5.5, an unnumbered paragraph gives the exact necessity witness — diag(1,2) and $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\0&-1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ diagonalisable with non-diagonalisable sum. It has no disposition row, and the harvest already rows unnumbered observations elsewhere.

**The notes contradict themselves on a field step 5 writes.** Line 159 tags `ex-primary-decomposition-over-q-…` `literature-derived`; line 327 of the same file says it must be `ai-altered`. Only the appended narrative was corrected — the failure shape inside the corrective pass.

**A miss of mine on page 94.** `def-gram-matrix-and-gram-determinant` and `thm-gram-determinant-detects-linear-independence` are tagged `literature-derived`, and "Gram matrix"/"Gram determinant" occur **0 times** in the whole 404-page Axler and 0 times in Treil Ch. 5 (all 23 "Gram" hits are Gram–Schmidt). In round 1 I checked page 94's replacement rows and not its unrowed items. It doesn't block the splice, but don't let step 5 write Axler as the reference for them.

Also: **`research/frontier-13-batch-1.coverage.json` carries the same dead Knapp URL** — outside my scope, but the fix3 rationale leaned on batch 1 having verified it live. And `tools/url-sweep.mjs` exists and does exactly this job, but its only caller is `run-wave.mjs`, the audit driver; the build never runs it, and it takes manifests and ledgers rather than a `coverage.json`.
